A brother to top class performers Baaeed and Hukum, Raaheeb began his career perfectly with a nice success at two, before taking the Classic Trial at Sandown in terrific fashion. He then ran creditably when fourth in the Irish Derby, travelling up like a genuine challenger before tiring late under Rossa Ryan. The time given to help Raaheeb develop physically and mentally could set him up for a nice return to the track and he should be tough to beat in calmer waters, even under a penalty. metadata.summary: Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague.
metadata.content: Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague Littler beats Humphries 8-6 in final after beating Michael van Gerwen, Danny Noppert and Krzysztof Ratajski earlier on Sunday; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4 Sunday 6 September 2026 23:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler claimed the Czech Darts Open with a win over Luke Humphries. Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague. Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year. Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16. messages.text: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller

metadata.summary: Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a  13½-12½ scoreline.
metadata.content: Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest USA missed four putts to retain the trophy after whitewashing Great Britain and Ireland in the morning foursomes; Watch the first round of the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage starting on Thursday September 10 from 1:30pm Sunday 6 September 2026 22:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Walker Cup held at the Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline. Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of losses in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches. But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory. The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup. Carty dramatically toppled through the ropes after being hit on the back of the head in the opening round of his clash with Allen on the undercard of Katie Taylor's farewell fight at Croke Park on Saturday.
